I have this discussion with my husband on a fairly regular basis. I love the convenience and portability of my Kindle compared to lugging around a stack of books all the time. I love that I can hop onto my local library's website and download any borrow any e-book that I want whenever I want. I wish I could have a home library full of every book I've ever wanted, but eBooks are just so much easier.
eBook vs Actual Book -- What is your choice and why?
+1 for Kindle. EBooks are just so much more practical. The only books I prefer to have a dead tree version of are heavily illustrated ones.
I use a Kindle Paperwhite and I love it - It fits in my pocket, I'm not distracted by apps and the internet, and it isn't a glossy screen.
I have a Kindle Touch myself. It's very easy on the eyes, light and portable. The Amazon integration is a blessing and a curse I guess, with 1-click shopping it's way too easy to buy new books =/
I use the Moon Reader app on my phone. My phone is always with me so I can read any time, anywhere, without having to carry anything else with me.
Definitely ebooks! I usually read while nursing my son to bed and then I read after he's fallen asleep. That would be impossible to do with a real book!

I prefer print books. It's much nicer having something solid in your hand that isn't a screen. You also never need to charge a print book. One huge reason I don't like e-books is the way publishers can control them. Once a print book was purchased by a library, there were no limits on how many times it could be checked out. The publisher had no say in what the library did with the book once they got it. Now, publishers can limit the number of times a book can be checked out, and require the library to repurchase the book. Another huge issue is that the book is never truly yours. Amazon can't come and take away books off my shelf after I bought them. But if they get into a disagreement with a publisher, poof, all those ebooks are gone off your device.

Here's one article on it: https://www.techdirt.com/articles/20101215/02571612282/another-reminder-that-you-dont-own-your-ebooks-amazon-removing-more-ebooks-you-bought-archives.shtml

Another: http://bits.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/02/22/amazon-pulls-thousands-of-e-books-in-dispute/

I love the thought of ebooks, I own a Kindle DX ( only wanted an ebook, not something to surf the intertubes with ). I tend to just 'scan' things on electronic screens, hence the e-ink display. I only use it for learning-type books ( textbooks, manuals, etc ) and anything else, I'll try to purchase used or old.

My brain reads books better when I can turn the pages. Disclosure, I'm 36. Maybe the young kids can cope with this disparity better - it's hard for me to read, word for word, a book where I can't turn the pages. Make me an e-book that I can at least turn a page or two - and you will sell one to not only myself, but another 30+ million other people in my age group or older.

I still use e-books for traveling, but it's a pain to go through; I need more breaks, and not just due to eye-fatigue ( e-ink doesn't do that ), but I just want to 'scan' the page when it seems 'digital'.

That's my $.02
